Lines before the first snippet are not assembled.

Cases llvm-mc refuses to assemble, checked against GNU as instead. `adrp` of
a symbol with an absolute value takes that address's page, while `adrp` of a
bare number counts pages from here. (GNU as 2.47 has an internal error on
`:lo12:` of a bare number, so the load names a `.set` symbol.)

The literal pools are here too: llvm-mc has none, and a pool is laid out
across a whole section, so only a linked image shows where its entries went
and which of them the loads share.

=== adrp and :lo12: of absolute addresses @ 0x400ff8
        .set    konst, 0x12345
        .set    slot, 0x5008
        nop
        adrp    x0, konst
        add     x0, x0, :lo12:konst
        adrp    x1, 0x5000
        adrp    x4, -0x3000
        ldr     x2, [x1, :lo12:slot]
        adrp    x3, 0x400000

=== a literal pool at the end of the section, with symbols in it
entry:  ldr     x0, =entry
        ldr     w1, =msg
        ldr     x2, =msg + 3
        ldr     x3, =0x123456789
        ldr     w4, =0x12345678
        ldr     x5, =0x123456789
        ret
        .data
msg:    .ascii  "hello"

=== a pool placed by ltorg, and a second one after it
entry:  ldr     x0, =table
        b       over
        .ltorg
over:   ldr     x1, =table + 4
        ldr     x2, =0xdeadbeefcafe
        ldr     s3, =0x3fc00000
        ret
        .section .rodata
        .byte   1
table:  .word   1, 2, 3

=== a constant that would fit an immediate still goes in the pool
entry:  ldr     x0, =0
        ldr     x1, =0xffff
        ldr     w2, =-1
        ldr     x3, =0x1234000000000000
        ldr     x4, =0xffffffffffff0000
        ldr     x5, =0x5555555555555555
        ldr     x6, =0x5555555555555556
        ret
